title: SHAPr: An Efficient and Versatile Membership Privacy Risk Metric for Machine Learning
sections_checked: §III-D: no demonstrably optimal MIA for metric ground truth
§VI, especially Table V: recall against modified-entropy and likelihood-ratio attacks
evidence_note: The authors evaluate SHAPr and SPRS against two concrete attacks on ten datasets. SHAPr often has high recall against the stronger likelihood-ratio attack (e.g. table reports 0.97–1.00 for most listed datasets), while comparison with the modified-entropy attack varies by dataset and can favor SPRS. Crucially, §III-D states that without a demonstrably optimal MIA, risk metrics can only be evaluated with respect to specific attacks. This both strengthens evidence for cross-dataset utility and narrows any universal attack-agnostic claim; it does not invalidate the metric.

title: Effects of Differential Privacy and Data Skewness on Membership Inference Vulnerability
sections_checked: §VI-C controlled CIFAR-10 minority representation and LFW subgroup evaluation
evidence_note: The paper reports group-specific attack results beyond aggregate accuracy. In its LFW evaluation, aggregate attack accuracy is 70.14%, versus 89.90% for racial-minority images and 76.85% for female images (non-disjoint subgroup definitions). The authors also vary minority-class representation in Adult and CIFAR-10 experiments. These results motivate subgroup reporting but remain tied to the paper's datasets, models, group definitions, and attack procedure; they are not a universal disparity estimate or independent validation of DTP/SHAPr.
